teacher: Matsunami Goro (Hero name: 'Scaffold' — Quirk: Construct, builds rigid scaffolding structures from ambient minerals. Methodical, patient, and quietly competitive about his class.)
reputation: The class that almost made it to 1-A. Their entrance exam scores were comparable — in some technical categories, better. Matsunami runs a tighter ship than Oshiro. 1-B students know their fundamentals cold before they start improvising. Less chaos, more precision. They watch 1-A the way you watch someone doing something impressive badly.
sports_festival_note: Tier 2, Arc 1. Class 1-B enter the Sports Festival as the school's open secret — everyone's picked a 1-A favourite, nobody's thought hard about 1-B. That's exactly how Matsunami wants it. He has drilled his students on 1-A's quirks from the entrance exam footage. This is the arc where 1-B stops being background noise.
dm_overview: 1-B shows up in pieces through Tier 1 — Morida's tray geometrically arranged in the cafeteria, Yashiro's wink across the room, Ogiwara's 7am warmup shaking the building two floors up. None of them are villains. None of them are friends yet, either — they're the specific kind of rival that makes a class sharper just by existing a few doors down. Morida's already logged Class 1-A's exam scores from memory. Kitamura's already three days into an internship the class hasn't started thinking about. By the Sports Festival, 1-B isn't a name on a bracket anymore — it's Morida, Yashiro, Ogiwara, Kitamura, and nobody in 1-A is sure who's actually going to win.

tier1_introduction_guide.arc1_entrance_exam: The results board after the exam shows Class 1-A and 1-B scores in adjacent columns. 1-B's top score (Morida: 84 pts) is visible. Whether it beats or matches 1-A's best depends on the session. Fujisaki mentions '1-B had a different site this year — quieter, but thorough.' Oshiro says nothing about 1-B. He doesn't need to.
tier1_introduction_guide.arc2_dorm_life: Morida and Yashiro are visible in the cafeteria. Morida's tray is geometrically arranged. He looks at the 1-A table once, says nothing. Yashiro catches the eye of whoever's watching and winks. The practice room booking shows 1-B has 6am slots every weekday. Ogiwara's warmup shakes the building at 7am. The class notices.
tier1_introduction_guide.arc3_capture_the_flag: Ogiwara is watching through the observation window. When a student looks over, he gives a slow thumbs up. It's impossible to tell if it's sincere or condescending. Oshiro drops the line: 'Class 1-B had three students who topped this score in their equivalent drill. That's your benchmark.'
tier1_introduction_guide.arc4_agency_visit: Kitamura Sora is at the same agency district for a different internship. If the class encounters her: she's carrying precisely folded documents, gives the impression she's been there three days, and has a 10-second corridor interaction before continuing. She doesn't introduce herself. Her name badge faces inward. If a student catches a glimpse: Kitamura, S., Class 1-B.

students.name: Morida Takeshi

quirk_mechanics.weakness: His hardened form can only absorb a limited amount of damage before it shatters, ending the effect and returning him to normal — any damage taken beyond his absorption limit carries over to his normal form.

abilities.name: Harden
abilities.description: Turns his skin to stone, gaining resistance to all damage types (except necrotic, psychic, and poison) for minutes equal to half his Constitution modifier. As a reaction, can move up to half his speed to intercept an incoming attack on an ally's behalf. Creatures within 10 ft directly behind him gain half cover.

abilities.name: Stone Weapon
abilities.description: Fists become blades (slashing) or solid stone fists (bludgeoning), dealing 1d10 + Strength modifier damage. Once per turn on a hit, deals bonus Xd4 damage (X = half Constitution modifier, rounded down). Gains +1 AC.

abilities.name: Re-Harden
abilities.description: If his Harden threshold is breached, regains 10 HP instantly; usable up to five times in one reaction. After using it, falls unconscious for rounds equal to the number of uses beyond the first. Once per short rest.

abilities.name: Unbreakable
abilities.description: Hardens his entire body for 4 rounds, becoming immune to all damage except necrotic, psychic, and poison, and granting total cover to allies directly behind him. Gains piercing damage and a climbing speed. Falls unconscious for 3 rounds and gains three levels of exhaustion afterward.

students.quirk_summary: Full-body metallic plating. Morida's skin hardens into dense, layered steel armour that he can extend or retract at will. At full hardening he's nearly impervious to physical attacks. At partial hardening he trades some protection for mobility. He cannot harden his eyes — his one consistent weak point.
students.personality: Disciplined, methodical, and quietly contemptuous of flashy quirk use. He respects results and is suspicious of anything he can't measure. Doesn't talk during a fight. Will compliment a student after if they earned it — which sounds like 'That was efficient.' He means it as high praise.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Engine vs Wall. Izuto's raw output vs Morida's near-absolute defence. The central question is whether Izuto can generate enough force to crack the armour before Morida just outlasts him. Morida has already figured out Izuto's timing. Izuto hasn't thought about Morida at all yet.
students.sports_festival_role: The unmovable object in direct contests. Morida's goal in every event is to simply not be eliminated. He doesn't need points — he needs to still be standing when everyone else isn't. He and Izuto will meet in the tournament bracket. That fight is the centrepiece of the Sports Festival arc.
students.tier1_appearance: Cafeteria during dorm move-in. Perfectly level tray. Makes eye contact with no one. Once, in the corridor, he passes Izuto without acknowledging him. Izuto doesn't notice. Morida does.
students.dm_notes: Morida is not a villain and not a bad person. He's the structural version of Masahata — someone who sees everything as a competition and is usually right about where everyone stands. Let him be correct. Let his correctness be slightly annoying. The payoff is at the Sports Festival when his certainty runs into Izuto's stubbornness.
signature_moves: Iron Stance: as a bonus action, increase AC by 2 until start of next turn (total AC 20). Speed drops to 0.
Armour Crash: full hardening bull rush — move 20ft in a line, +6 to hit, 2d8+3 bludgeoning, DC 14 STR save or knocked prone. Recharge 5-6.
Selective Hardening: can harden specific body parts — hardened fist deals +1d6 on a hit. Always on.

students.name: Yashiro Fumiko

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Part of her real body must be present to release the dark fog, exposing her to attack. Portals are coordinate-based, requiring her to know the exact location or have a clear line of sight, and she cannot create portals in heavy winds.

abilities.name: Portal Creation
abilities.description: Creates a number of 20-ft diameter portals up to her Proficiency Bonus within 30 feet, connecting to any location she can see or for which she has precise coordinates. Each portal lasts up to one minute or until dismissed. As a reaction, she can close a portal as a creature attempts to move through it — that creature makes a Dexterity save against her Quirk DC or takes 3d10 damage and is pushed back 10 feet.

abilities.name: Fog Shroud
abilities.description: Envelops herself in dark fog, becoming heavily obscured for one minute. While shrouded she can create portals as a bonus action, and attacks against her while obscured have disadvantage.

students.quirk_summary: Short-range teleportation. Yashiro can teleport up to 10 ft in any direction as a free action. Longer jumps (up to 30ft) require a bonus action and a 3-round cooldown. She can't blink through solid objects but can blink around corners she can see around. She uses this continuously and casually, which is deeply disorienting to fight.
students.personality: Smug, playful, treats combat like a game she's already won. Finds 1-A's chaos endearing in the way that people find puppies endearing — they're trying so hard. Genuinely likes competition. Would rather lose a good fight than win a boring one. Her competitive sincerity is the thing that catches people off guard — they expect cheap tricks and get instead a student who is actually, seriously fast.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Speed vs Evasion. Ren is faster in a straight line. Yashiro can't be chased in one. The question is whether Ren can close to a range where his attacks land before she blinks out. She's studied his Overclock pattern. He doesn't know she exists yet.
students.sports_festival_role: The worst person to be paired against in any containment event — she just isn't there. She's going to be in the tournament bracket and her match against Ren is the one that players will talk about afterwards regardless of who wins.
students.tier1_appearance: First spotted vanishing around a corner that didn't have a turn in it. If a student catches her eye in the cafeteria, she winks and blinks to three seats over without using the gap.
students.dm_notes: Yashiro is genuinely fun to run. She should feel slippery and quick, not cheap. There's always a clear solution to fighting her — the 3-round cooldown on long jumps, the can't-blink-through-solids rule — but finding it under pressure is hard. She and Ren actually like each other by the end of the Festival. Neither admits it.
signature_moves: Blink Step (Free): teleport up to 10 ft as part of movement. Can do this each turn without cost.
Long Jump (Bonus action): teleport up to 30ft. 3-round cooldown.
Phantom Strike: teleports adjacent to a target, attacks, then blinks 10ft away as part of the same action. Doesn't provoke opportunity attacks from that target.

students.name: Denma Ryusei

quirk_mechanics.weakness: His fingers must be exposed to use the Quirk, and prolonged use risks collateral damage — a failed save against Black Hole within 10 feet of fragile structures may cause them to collapse. While his fingers are exposed, ranged attacks against him within 10 feet have disadvantage and loose objects under 50 pounds drift toward him.

abilities.name: Black Hole
abilities.description: Creates a gravitational pulse in a 30-ft cone. Each creature makes a Strength save against his Quirk DC, taking 2d8 force damage and being pulled 15 feet closer on a fail, or half damage on a success. A creature ending its turn within 5 feet of him after a failed save becomes Restrained, taking 2d8 force damage at the start of each turn until it saves again.

abilities.name: Singularity Vortex
abilities.description: Creates a miniature black hole at a point within 60 feet for 1 minute. Each creature starting its turn within 15 feet makes a Strength save or is pulled 10 feet closer and takes 6d8 force damage (half on success). The area is difficult terrain and ranged attacks through it have disadvantage. Can be moved up to 20 feet as a bonus action.

abilities.name: Micro Collapse
abilities.description: Can disintegrate up to 50 pounds of non-living material (metal, stone, wood) by focusing the black hole, useful for disarming or destroying small unattended items or weakened constructs.

students.quirk_summary: Creates localised gravitational anomalies. Denma can designate a 10ft sphere within 60ft as either a high-gravity zone (things pulled toward its centre) or a low-gravity zone (things float away from it). Maintaining a zone requires concentration. He can have two zones active simultaneously at full concentration, but cannot attack while doing so.
students.personality: Quiet. Unsettling. Speaks in short declarative sentences and rarely finishes thoughts that the other person can follow anyway. Not cold — just somewhere else most of the time. Will talk at length about gravitational physics and the difference between mass and weight in a way that is technically correct and socially obliterating. The moments where he's actually paying attention to a person are rare and feel significant.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Both manipulate the battlefield rather than dealing direct damage. Chozen builds stress, breaks people down. Denma controls movement, removes options. Their rivalry is philosophical more than physical — two students who win through mechanism rather than power. At the Festival: both will try to make the other fight on their terms. Neither will fully succeed.
students.sports_festival_role: The wildcard in every group event. His zones control the field in ways that benefit teammates and punish enemies. In the tournament bracket, he's dangerous specifically because he doesn't need to beat you — he just needs you to be in the wrong place. Almost everyone underestimates the range.
students.tier1_appearance: A practice room booking under 1-B's name. Inside: twelve thumbtacks floating 2mm off the board, perfectly static. No explanation. The room smells faintly of ozone.
students.dm_notes: Denma is designed to be memorable through strangeness rather than threat. His encounters in Tier 1 should be brief and odd — a glance, a sentence, something not quite right about gravity in his vicinity. Save his actual fighting capability for the Festival. He should feel like a puzzle that hasn't been asked yet.
signature_moves: Gravity Zone (Action): designate a 10ft sphere within 60ft as high-gravity (creatures pulled to centre, speed halved) or low-gravity (creatures float up 5ft, speed halved in different axis). Concentration, 1 minute.
Dual Field: maintain two zones simultaneously. Cannot attack or take bonus actions while sustaining both.
Crush Point: collapse a high-gravity zone onto a single target. DC 14 STR save or restrained for 1 round and takes 2d6 force damage. Destroys the zone.

students.name: Ogiwara Bunta

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Prolonged use strains his muscles and joints — after using Big Fist a number of times equal to his level times his proficiency bonus, he must make a DC 13 Constitution save or take 1d12 true damage.

abilities.name: Giant Strength
abilities.description: Strength score maximum becomes 22, and carrying capacity is doubled.

abilities.name: Giant Punch
abilities.description: Enlarges a hand and strikes all creatures in a 10-ft long, 10-ft wide line, dealing 2d12 bludgeoning damage and producing a wind shock that pushes targets back 15 feet.

abilities.name: Ground Pound
abilities.description: Slams an enlarged hand into the ground. All creatures within a 20-ft radius make a Dexterity save or take 4d12 bludgeoning damage and are knocked prone; the area becomes difficult terrain.

students.quirk_summary: Ogiwara can enlarge either hand to enormous size, vastly increasing his striking power and reach. A straight punch becomes a battering ram that flattens anything in a line; slammed into the ground it sends a shockwave of displaced air and debris radiating outward. Scaling: a standard Giant Punch hits everything in a 10-ft line. A full Ground Pound clears a 20-ft radius and leaves the area difficult terrain. Doesn't work if his hand can't reach the target or the ground.
students.personality: Loud. Genuinely, physically loud — his voice carries without him trying. Enthusiastic competitor in the way that makes it fun to lose to him because he's so happy about having a real contest. No subtlety. No hidden agenda. Will shake your hand and mean it. Will also absolutely try to put you through the floor.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Sound vs Big Fist. Both create broad-area chaos. Both are physically enormous and running at things is their default strategy. They'll either be best friends or destroy each other immediately at the Festival — the exact circumstances of their first meeting will determine which. Either outcome is correct.
students.sports_festival_role: Devastating in group events that require movement or terrain control. In the tournament bracket, he's the crowd favourite — his Giant Punch and Ground Pound create visible, dramatic shockwaves that the audience loves. Weakness: if someone gets him airborne or out of arm's reach, his quirk is useless. Not a weakness he's addressed.
students.tier1_appearance: Two 7am shockwaves on move-in morning, felt through the dorm floor. If confronted: 'Warmup.' Delivered as a complete explanation. Gives the thumbs up through the Capture the Flag observation window — entirely genuine, completely unreadable.
students.dm_notes: Ogiwara is the relief. Run every Tier 1 scene with him as a moment of levity. He has no secrets, no agenda, no hidden depth to excavate. His arc at the Sports Festival is uncomplicated: he wants to test himself against Toshida. Give him that fight and let it be excellent.
signature_moves: Giant Punch (Scaled): enlarges a hand and strikes everything in a 10-ft line. 2d10 bludgeoning damage and a wind-shock push of 10 feet.
Ground Pound (Scaled): slams an enlarged hand into the ground. 15-ft radius, 3d10 bludgeoning, DC 14 DEX save or knocked prone. Difficult terrain left behind. Recharge 5-6.
Giant Strength (Passive): his Strength score maximum is treated as 22, and his carrying capacity is doubled.

students.name: Nashiro Aoi

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Physical contact is required to copy a Quirk, and each copied power fades after two minutes. Accumulation- or mutation-based Quirks cannot be properly replicated, and upon copying she inherits all of its drawbacks, requiring a successful DC 16 Athletics check — on a failure, she cannot attempt to copy that specific Quirk again for seven rounds.

abilities.name: Mimic Touch
abilities.description: When she lands an unarmed strike on a creature, she may copy their Quirk. The copied Quirk lasts two minutes (three at 5th level, five at 10th level).

abilities.name: Quirk Swap
abilities.description: Switches between stored copied Quirks. She may maintain up to two copied Quirks at once, increasing by one additional Quirk at 5th and 10th level.

students.quirk_summary: Nashiro can borrow a Quirk by landing a hit on its user — for two minutes she has full use of whatever ability they're carrying, layered over (or instead of) her own approach to a fight. She's spent years cataloguing how other people's powers actually work in practice, which means she rarely copies something she doesn't already know how to use well. She cannot copy mutation- or accumulation-based Quirks, and copying anything risky means inheriting its drawbacks too.
students.personality: Theatrical. Observant in the way that only people who spend a lot of time watching other people are. In public she's performing — always, slightly, a version of herself edited for the room. In private (which almost never happens with 1-A) she's dry and tired in an interesting way. She's been reading Class 1-A since the results board, cataloguing every Quirk she's seen on tape and deciding which would actually be worth taking from them in a fight.
students.rivalry_dynamic: The obvious play for Nashiro against Steel is to land a hit and copy it — except copying Kazama barely helps her on its own. She'd still have to land that hit while he's hardened and absorbing exactly the kind of damage she's trying to dish out, then spend two minutes being just as hard to put down as he already is. Kazama knows this, which means the real fight is about whether she can find an opening before he hardens, or simply outlast his daily uses. Kazama doesn't know she exists yet. Their Sports Festival match, if it happens, is a patience game — whoever blinks first.
students.sports_festival_role: Nightmarish in group events that involve direct confrontation — she can absorb whoever hits her first and turn their own Quirk against the rest of the field. In the tournament bracket, she's a puzzle encounter: students need to avoid giving her a clean touch while she's actively hunting for the most dangerous Quirk on the field to borrow.
students.tier1_appearance: A 1-A student swears Hamagawa tagged them with a light shove in a sparring drill, then suddenly fought like Hamagawa for thirty seconds. It wasn't Hamagawa. Nobody can prove it was Nashiro. If directly confronted: 'I don't know what you're referring to.' She says it with Hamagawa's exact dry cadence.
students.dm_notes: Nashiro is a slow-burn reveal. Her Tier 1 appearances should all be deniable — a tagged opponent briefly fighting unlike themselves, easy to write off as imagination. By the Sports Festival, players should be actively wary of letting her land a hit, which is exactly where she wants them.
signature_moves: Mimic Touch (Bonus action): on landing an unarmed strike, copy the target's Quirk. Lasts two minutes. Cannot copy mutation- or accumulation-based Quirks, and inherits the copied Quirk's drawbacks.
Quirk Swap (Bonus action): switches which copied Quirk is currently active. Can hold up to two copied Quirks in reserve at once.
Cold Read (Passive): from prior observation of an opponent's Quirk in use, she has advantage on the Athletics check required when first copying it.

students.name: Kitamura Sora

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Deploying a full network takes several seconds and requires anchor points (walls, fixtures, the ground) within range — in a completely open space with nothing to anchor to, she has nothing to work with. Destroying enough of the network in one area collapses her coverage there.

abilities.name: Wire Network
abilities.description: Deploys near-invisible tripwire filaments across a 30-ft radius area within 60 feet, anchored to available surfaces. For as long as the network is up (concentration, up to 10 minutes), she knows the exact position of every creature that has moved through it, and can reveal the wires as a bonus action to make each entangled creature make a Dexterity save or become restrained.

abilities.name: Snap Line
abilities.description: When a restrained creature within her Wire Network attempts to break free, she can retract a section of wire to deal 2d8 slashing damage to it instead of allowing an automatic escape attempt.

students.quirk_summary: Kitamura generates and controls thin, incredibly strong filament wire from her fingertips, which she strings across a space faster than most people can register it's happening. Once a network is up, she knows exactly where everyone in it is and how they're moving — tension vectors, weight shifts, the works — without needing to see them directly. Setting up a full-coverage network in a room takes her approximately four seconds. She has timed this.
students.personality: Precise. Economical. Considers Class 1-A's operational style inefficient in the way an architect considers a building that keeps falling down. She isn't contemptuous — she's concerned, professionally. Has extremely strong opinions about workspace organisation and does not volunteer them unsolicited. Will volunteer them if asked. Has very few opinions about things she considers not her domain. Says 'Yes.' and 'No.' as complete sentences.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Lightning vs Wire. Kitamura's filament is metal, and metal conducts beautifully — if Nakaya lands a single arc on any strand of an active network, the whole thing lights up and Kitamura loses it instantly rather than gradually. Kitamura's counter is speed: she has to sense Nakaya closing in and pull the network before contact, which turns their matchups into Kitamura staying one wire ahead of a girl who just needs to touch anything metal. Their rivalry is about Kitamura learning that a sensing network is also a liability if the thing it senses can hit back through it.
students.sports_festival_role: Devastating in any event with structure — she pre-rigs environments with wire during setup phases. In group contests, she's invisible until suddenly four students are tracked and tangled simultaneously. In the tournament bracket, she's the student everyone is afraid to face because they've seen her work and don't know where the wire is.
students.tier1_appearance: Corridor encounter during the Agency Visit arc. 10 seconds. She's carrying precisely folded documents, doesn't introduce herself, continues walking. Her name badge faces inward. If a student catches a glimpse: Kitamura, S., 1-B. The practice room she used before leaving has wire patterns still strung across it at odd angles — easy to miss until someone almost walks into one.
students.dm_notes: Kitamura is the student who makes players feel like they've been outplayed by something they didn't see coming. Her Tier 1 presence should be minimal and precise — the corridor encounter, the wire patterns. Nothing else. By the Sports Festival, her reputation has been built entirely by absence. The fight against her should be the one that makes players think hard about the environment before they enter it.
signature_moves: Wire Network (Action, concentration): deploys a 30-ft radius tripwire field for up to 10 minutes. Tracks every creature that moves through it.
Tension Read (Passive): advantage on Perception/Insight against anyone inside an active network; cannot be surprised by them.
Snap Line (Reaction): deals 2d8 slashing damage to a restrained creature attempting to escape the network instead of allowing a free attempt.

students.name: Hatsuda Renko

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Requires a precise touch — a grapple, a restrained target, or anything that keeps her from making clean contact prevents the burst from forming properly, and each burst leaves her fingertips numb for a round afterward.

abilities.name: Tap
abilities.description: Touches a creature, releasing a concentrated burst of compressed air at the point of contact. Target makes a Constitution save or takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage and is pushed 10 feet directly away from her (half damage, not pushed, on a success).

abilities.name: Chain Tap
abilities.description: If her last Tap this turn hit, she can immediately Tap a second creature within 5 feet of the first, at disadvantage.

students.quirk_summary: Hatsuda can compress the air at a single point of contact into a concentrated, invisible burst — a tap on the shoulder that lands like a punch, a handshake that knocks someone back a full stride. It's precise, it's fast, and it means she's constantly thinking about who's in reach and in what order, the same restless calculation she brings to everything else.
students.personality: Restless, fidgety, talks fast when she's nervous and faster when she's not. Treats every space she enters as a tactical map of who's within arm's reach — railings, doorways, crowded corridors — without really meaning to. Funny in a way that lands half the time. The other half she's already moved on to the next thought before anyone's caught up.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Water Gun vs Pressure Point. Masahata's ranged blasts keep distance between them — exactly the range where Hatsuda's touch-based quirk does nothing at all. The whole fight is about whether she can close the gap before he's put enough water between them that she never gets a single Tap in.
students.sports_festival_role: Lethal in close-quarters events where opponents can't keep her at range. In the tournament bracket, the smart play against her is distance — most opponents don't think to keep it until she's already closed on them once.
students.tier1_appearance: A 1-A student high-fives Hatsuda in the hallway and stumbles back a full step, more startled than hurt. Hatsuda apologises without sounding sorry, already three thoughts ahead about who else is in reach.
students.dm_notes: Hatsuda's threat is entirely about closing distance and reading who's reachable. Tier 1 should establish that she's always calculating who's in arm's reach. Her match against Masahata at the Festival should hinge on whether he can keep range on her long enough for it to matter.
signature_moves: Tap (Action): touch attack. CON save or 2d8 bludgeoning damage and pushed 10 feet.
Chain Tap (Bonus Action, 5th level): after a hit, taps a second target within 5 feet at disadvantage.
Fingertip Control (Passive): can scale Tap's force down to be nonlethal and harmless at will, useful outside combat.

students.name: Fujikawa Renta

quirk_mechanics.weakness: His increased mass means falling or unstable surfaces become a serious hazard — he can crack or collapse flooring not built to hold his weight, and being forcibly moved while at full mass deals him an extra 1d6 damage from the sheer inertia involved.

abilities.name: Full Mass
abilities.description: Compacts his body's density to several times normal for one minute. Gains advantage on Strength checks and saves and automatically succeeds saves against being moved or knocked prone, but speed is reduced by 15 feet.

abilities.name: Dead Weight Strike
abilities.description: Unarmed strikes deal 1d10 + Strength modifier bludgeoning damage, and on a hit the target must succeed on a Strength save or be knocked prone by the sheer mass behind the blow.

abilities.name: Anchor
abilities.description: While at Full Mass, grants advantage on a single Strength check or save made to resist being moved, grappled, or shoved — usable even outside his turn.

students.quirk_summary: Fujikawa can compact his own body's density to several times normal, becoming immensely heavy without changing shape or appearance — no metal skin, no visible transformation, just a person who suddenly weighs as much as a car. Once he's settled his weight, moving him takes actual physics, not effort. He treats this as an honest deal rather than a flaw: total commitment, total stillness, total presence.
students.personality: Stoic to the point of being mistaken for boring, which he finds mildly amusing. Has an old-fashioned sense of duty about being the class's anchor in group events. Doesn't volunteer opinions about other people's quirks but will defend Morida's methods to anyone who calls 1-B's style 'rigid.' Plays a lot of shogi against himself between classes.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Vines vs Ballast is patience against patience — Kibi can bind and constrict, but binding something whose weight alone breaks most anchoring points buys Fujikawa time he's happy to spend. The fight, if it happens, is a long one and neither of them minds that.
students.sports_festival_role: An anchor in any event requiring someone to hold a position or absorb sustained pressure. Slow enough that speed-based opponents can simply outrun him — a gap he knows about and has made peace with rather than solved.
students.tier1_appearance: Seen in the practice yard standing motionless at Full Mass for the full one-minute duration, timing himself with a stopwatch. The floor tile beneath him has a fine crack radiating outward that nobody's mentioned yet.
students.dm_notes: Fujikawa is a straightforward wall-archetype with one clean exploitable weakness — speed. Use him as a teaching encounter for kiting tactics. His rivalry with Kibi should be a slow, almost friendly war of attrition rather than a dramatic clash.
signature_moves: Full Mass (Bonus Action): compacts for one minute. Advantage on STR checks/saves, automatically succeeds against forced movement, speed -15 ft.
Dead Weight Strike: while at Full Mass, unarmed strikes deal 1d10 + STR bludgeoning damage and a failed STR save knocks the target prone.
Anchor (Reaction): while at Full Mass, grants advantage on a save/check to resist being moved, grappled, or shoved.

students.name: Soga Mitsuru

quirk_mechanics.weakness: The effect only works on creatures who aren't already focused directly on him — anyone actively engaged with him in melee combat, or who has succeeded a save against him in the last minute, sees him perfectly and cannot be affected again for 24 hours.

abilities.name: Slip Notice
abilities.description: For one minute, becomes difficult to notice — attacks against him have disadvantage from any creature that hasn't already targeted him this fight, and he doesn't provoke opportunity attacks while moving.

abilities.name: Nobody Here
abilities.description: Emits a pulse in a 15-foot radius. Each creature that has not already saved against him this encounter makes a Wisdom save or completely loses track of his location for 1 round, treating the space he's in as empty even if directly looking at it.

students.quirk_summary: Soga isn't invisible — he's unremarkable in a very specific, quirk-powered way. People's attention simply doesn't catch on him, the way you don't notice a familiar hallway or a person who's 'supposed' to be there. It stops working the moment someone actually engages him directly; commit to fighting him and the effect breaks entirely. He's spent a long time thinking about the exact borderline between 'unnoticed' and 'not present,' and he's very precise about which side of it he's standing on.
students.personality: Quiet, watchful, faintly amused by how much other people worry about doors. Doesn't see the point of confrontation when he can simply not be where the confrontation is. This makes him hard to provoke and harder to actually fight. Has a dry running commentary he mostly keeps to himself.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Iron Claws vs Blind Spot. Aikawa hits hard and fast in close range — but she has to find him first, and find him again every time he resets the field. The entire fight is Aikawa learning that the moment she actually engages him, the trick is gone for good, and Soga learning that eventually somebody commits and he has to actually be somewhere.
students.sports_festival_role: A nightmare for point-based or capture events — judges and opponents alike keep losing track of where he is entirely. In the tournament bracket, his weakness is exposed the moment an opponent successfully lands a hit or lock on him: after that, he's just a person standing in a ring like everyone else.
students.tier1_appearance: A hallway monitor reviews footage of an empty corridor and insists someone must have walked through it, because the door at the far end opens on its own. Soga is seen a minute later, several floors away, looking unbothered.
students.dm_notes: Soga should feel genuinely strange to fight — not stealthy in a cinematic sense, but structurally hard to keep track of until someone actually commits to him. Once a player succeeds a save or lands a hit, let him become fully, ordinarily present for the rest of that fight — that's the whole balance lever.
signature_moves: Slip Notice (Bonus Action): for one minute, attacks against him from anyone who hasn't already targeted him this fight have disadvantage; no opportunity attacks against him while moving.
Nobody Here (Action): 15-ft pulse. Creatures who haven't already saved against him this encounter make a WIS save or lose track of his location for 1 round.
Reset (Passive): once a creature saves against him or lands a hit, that creature sees him clearly for the rest of the encounter — the effect never reapplies to them.

students.name: Anrakuji Hisame

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Only works on things that will make sound — silent attacks, ranged weapons loosed without a telltale noise, or anything happening for the first time in total silence give her nothing to hear ahead of time.

abilities.name: Early Ear
abilities.description: When a creature within 30 feet is about to make an attack roll or loud action, she hears it fractions of a second before it happens, granting herself or an ally within 30 feet advantage on their next saving throw or AC-relevant check against it.

abilities.name: Playback
abilities.description: Concentrates to hear a few seconds into a single creature's immediate future within 60 feet, learning the general category of its next action (attack, movement, ability use) before it happens. Usable a number of times equal to her proficiency bonus per long rest.

students.quirk_summary: Anrakuji hears things before they make noise — a punch a half-second before impact, a shout before it's spoken, footsteps before the foot lands. It's not the future, exactly; it's an echo arriving early, and only for things that are going to be loud enough to hear. Silent things give her nothing. She's learned not to trust it for big decisions and to trust it completely for the next six seconds.
students.personality: Calm in a way that unsettles people who don't know why. Speaks carefully, like she's already heard the conversation once. Genuinely warm to people she trusts, which is a short list and entirely intentional. Hates being asked 'so what happens next' as a party trick — it doesn't work that way and she's tired of explaining it.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Iron Ball vs Echo. Setaka's attacks are heavy, telegraphed, and loud — exactly the kind of thing Anrakuji hears coming from a mile off. The real contest is whether he can land a hit quietly enough, or fast enough, that the sound arrives at the same moment as the blow instead of before it.
students.sports_festival_role: An incredible support piece in team events — warning allies a half-second before a loud hit lands changes outcomes constantly. In the tournament bracket, she's vulnerable to anyone whose attacks are naturally silent, which is rare but a real counter for the right opponent.
students.tier1_appearance: She tells a classmate to move a half-second before a dropped supply crate would have hit them. Doesn't explain. They thank her anyway, more confused than grateful.
students.dm_notes: Anrakuji is best run as a constant low-grade advantage rather than a flashy one — small warnings, redirected attacks, near-misses that look like luck. Keep the limitation (has to make noise) visible so smart players can find the counter.
signature_moves: Early Ear (Reaction): when a creature within 30ft is about to make an attack or loud action, grant advantage on the next save/AC-relevant check against it to herself or an ally.
Playback (Action): hear a creature's next action category a few seconds early. Limited uses per long rest.
Quiet Room (Passive): disadvantage on Stealth checks made against her by anyone who has made noise in the last minute.

students.name: Karube Genta

quirk_mechanics.weakness: The escalation must build over several rounds and cannot be triggered instantly — at the start of combat he is at his weakest, and anything that resets his focus (being stunned, losing concentration) sends the buildup back to zero.

abilities.name: Rising Heat
abilities.description: At the start of each of his turns in combat, gains a stacking +1 bonus to Strength-based attack and damage rolls, to a maximum of +5 after five rounds.

abilities.name: Release
abilities.description: Expends all current Rising Heat stacks in a single attack, adding the full stacked bonus as additional damage on a hit, then resets stacks to zero.

students.quirk_summary: Karube's body builds toward its own peak the longer a fight runs — slow to start, terrifying by round five. Unlike a fixed strength boost, this is momentum: something in his output compounds turn over turn as long as nothing interrupts the escalation. The trade-off is brutal — anything that resets his focus (a stun, a hard knockdown, a long pause) sends him back to square one.
students.personality: Patient to a degree that frustrates faster classmates. Treats early-fight setbacks with total calm because he knows what round five looks like. Doesn't trash-talk. Will, however, very quietly count out loud when he's winning, which everyone finds more unnerving than any taunt.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Dupli-Arms vs Slow Burn. Samitsu's extra limbs let him overwhelm early with sheer action economy — precisely the window where Karube is weakest. If Samitsu can't close it out fast, round five arrives and the math flips hard in Karube's favour.
students.sports_festival_role: A slow-burn threat in any extended bout — the longer an event runs, the worse a proposition he becomes. In short, fast events he's mediocre, which the entrance exam scores reflected and which 1-A has no reason to suspect changes everything by round five.
students.tier1_appearance: Sparring drill footage shows him losing badly for the first four rounds and then ending it in two hits. Nobody who saw only the first half believes the second half happened.
students.dm_notes: Karube rewards players who either end fights fast or specifically target his concentration to reset his stacks. Telegraph the build clearly (describe the visible escalation each round) so the threat feels earned rather than arbitrary.
signature_moves: Rising Heat (Passive): +1 to STR attack/damage rolls at the start of each turn in combat, stacking to +5.
Release (Action): spends all stacks on one attack as bonus damage, then resets to zero.
Steady Pace (Passive): immune to being frightened; resets to zero on a failed concentration check instead of automatic loss.

students.name: Ezumi Wakana

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Her shards are limited in number — she carries a finite reserve that regrows only on a long rest — and each one that misses or is destroyed is gone until then. Against heavily armoured targets, shards that connect often lodge without penetrating deep enough to draw blood.

abilities.name: Shard Loose
abilities.description: Launches a spray of dense, needle-thin bone shards from her forearm at a target within 30 feet. On a hit, deals 1d10 piercing damage and the target begins Bleeding (1d4 at the start of each of its turns until treated).

abilities.name: Scatter Volley
abilities.description: Launches shards at up to three targets within 30 feet, each requiring a separate attack roll, dealing 1d6 piercing damage and a stack of Bleed on a hit.

abilities.name: Regrow
abilities.description: Recovers half her spent shard reserve on a short rest, and her full reserve on a long rest.

students.quirk_summary: Ezumi's body grows and sheds dense, needle-sharp bone shards from her forearms, which she can launch at range hard enough to punch through skin and lodge deep enough to keep bleeding. It looks unassuming until the first one lands — brutal for a straight-line attacker to see coming, and murder on unarmoured targets. She reads whether a target's likely to be worth the ammunition before she spends it.
students.personality: Sharp-tongued in exactly the way you'd expect, and aware enough of the joke to be tired of making it herself. Competitive in short bursts, then disinterested once she's proven her point. Genuinely kind to people who aren't currently in a fight with her.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Scales vs Splinter. Ando's natural armour is exactly the kind of surface her shards struggle to punch through cleanly — she has to find the gaps in his scales rather than blanketing him, which goes against every instinct she has for closing a fight fast.
students.sports_festival_role: Devastating against unarmoured opponents at range, considerably less so against anything hardened or plated where her shards can't punch deep enough to matter. In the tournament bracket, her matchups are extremely lopsided in one direction or the other.
students.tier1_appearance: A training dummy in the gym is found bristling with a dozen bone-white splinters, all clustered in a fist-sized area. The instructor says nothing, just adds another dummy to the supply order.
students.dm_notes: Ezumi is a glass-cannon against soft targets and a genuine puzzle against armoured ones. Lean into the read-your-opponent angle, and track her ammunition — running dry mid-fight should be a real, discoverable consequence.
signature_moves: Shard Loose (Action): ranged bone-shard attack, 30ft, 1d10 piercing damage and Bleed on a hit.
Scatter Volley (Action): launches shards at up to three targets within 30ft, 1d6 piercing and Bleed each on a hit.
Regrow (Passive): recovers half her spent shards on a short rest, all of them on a long rest.

students.name: Tsukikage Renji

quirk_mechanics.weakness: The afterimage is purely visual and offers no protection against attacks that don't rely on sight — and it only forms from movement, so standing still leaves him with nothing to hide behind.

abilities.name: Trailing Light
abilities.description: Whenever he moves at least 10 feet, leaves a faint, glowing duplicate of himself at his prior position for a few seconds.

abilities.name: Wrong Target
abilities.description: When targeted by an attack while an afterimage exists within 5 feet of him, forces the attacker to make a Wisdom save; on a failure, the attack instead strikes the afterimage and automatically misses.

abilities.name: Flood the Frame
abilities.description: Creates three afterimages simultaneously around himself that mimic his last few seconds of movement, each lasting one round.

students.quirk_summary: Tsukikage's body leaves a faint trail of light behind it when he moves — a lingering, glowing duplicate of where he just was, bright enough to read as 'him' for a half-second too long. He's spent years learning to move in ways that make the afterimage lie convincingly, misdirecting attacks toward the ghost instead of the person.
students.personality: Easygoing, a little dramatic, treats his own quirk like a stage light he gets to operate. Enjoys being the centre of attention in a literal sense and is fine with it being figurative too. Surprisingly tactical when it matters — the showmanship is real but it's not the whole picture.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Double vs Afterimage. Yoshibara's duplicate is a fully real, physical copy of her; Tsukikage's is a lie made of light with nothing behind it. The fight is about whether she can tell the difference between a fake that hits back and a fake that doesn't fast enough to matter — and whether he can keep moving convincingly enough that his trail keeps working.
students.sports_festival_role: Excellent in fast-paced, high-movement events where his trailing image keeps confusing pursuit. In the tournament bracket, opponents who stop trying to track him visually — sound, vibration, anything non-visual — cut straight through his biggest advantage.
students.tier1_appearance: The dorm hallway lights flicker out during a blackout drill and for a moment there are two Tsukikages at the end of the corridor, one of them fading gently, both equally unbothered.
students.dm_notes: Tsukikage's afterimage-only-from-movement clause is the built-in balance lever — make sure players learn it exists, ideally by him standing still and looking suddenly very exposed once in Tier 1.
signature_moves: Trailing Light (Passive): moving at least 10ft leaves a glowing afterimage at his prior position for a few seconds.
Wrong Target (Reaction): an attacker targeting him within 5ft of an active afterimage makes a WIS save or hits the afterimage instead, automatically missing.
Flood the Frame (Action, 5th level): creates three simultaneous afterimages mimicking his recent movement, each lasting one round.

students.name: Onogawa Subaru

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Requires both hands free and a clear line for the blast — grappled, restrained, or with only one hand free, he can't generate enough compression to matter. The blast has no effect on anything already braced or behind full cover.

abilities.name: Clap
abilities.description: Claps his hands together, releasing a burst of compressed air in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area makes a Strength save or takes 2d10 thunder damage and is pushed back 15 feet (half damage, not pushed, on a success).

abilities.name: Focused Report
abilities.description: Compresses the blast into a tight line instead of a cone — 30 feet long, 5 feet wide — dealing 3d10 thunder damage and forcing a Strength save or the target is also knocked prone.

students.quirk_summary: Onogawa can compress and release air between his palms hard enough to produce a directional shockwave — a clap that sounds like a gunshot and hits like one too. No contact needed, no surface required, just clear air in front of him and both hands free. He likes that it's loud. He likes that everyone in the room knows exactly when it happened.
students.personality: Blunt, a little gruff, says exactly what he thinks and is occasionally surprised when that lands badly. Respects effort over results, which makes him an easy training partner and a hard one to actually beat in his own estimation. Likes things that make satisfying noises.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Tail vs Concussive Clap. Isokono's tail gives him reach and balance Onogawa doesn't have — but the moment she closes to a range where the tail matters, she's well inside his blast cone. The fight comes down to whether Isokono can close that gap fast enough to matter before he gets both hands free and lined up.
students.sports_festival_role: Strong in any event that rewards controlling space at range — a clean Clap clears a doorway or a chokepoint instantly. In the tournament bracket, opponents who close to grappling range before he can line up a shot take that option away from him entirely.
students.tier1_appearance: A vending machine in the common room develops a hairline crack across the glass after Onogawa claps his hands to make a point during an argument, from ten feet away, without meaning to hit it.
students.dm_notes: Onogawa's vulnerability — grapple range and having a hand occupied — should be discoverable rather than announced. Let a smart player figure it out mid-fight. His rivalry with Isokono should hinge on closing distance as the explicit fail condition for his usual strategy.
signature_moves: Clap (Action): 15-ft cone of compressed air. STR save or 2d10 thunder damage and pushed back 15 feet.
Focused Report (Action, 5th level): 30-ft line, 5 ft wide. 3d10 thunder damage and a STR save or knocked prone.
Full Volume (Passive): creatures that fail their save against either ability are also deafened until the end of their next turn.

students.name: Mizuhana Kotori

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Effects require moisture already present in the air or ground nearby — in genuinely arid conditions she has very little to work with, and pulling too much moisture from an area too quickly leaves her lightheaded, imposing disadvantage on her next Constitution save.

abilities.name: Fogbank
abilities.description: Condenses moisture from the air into a thick fog filling a 20-ft radius zone within 60 feet for up to one minute (concentration). The area is heavily obscured.

abilities.name: Wring Dry
abilities.description: Within an active Fogbank, pulls all moisture from a 15-ft radius zone. Each creature in the area makes a Constitution save or takes 3d8 damage from sudden dehydration and gains a level of exhaustion (half damage, no exhaustion, on a success).

students.quirk_summary: Mizuhana can draw the moisture out of the air around her — thickening it into a rolling fog thick enough to blind a room, or pulling it out entirely until the air feels like a desert. It's slow to build and entirely dependent on staying focused, but a fully formed fogbank changes the terms of an entire fight, not just her part of it.
students.personality: Dreamy, unhurried, talks about weather the way other people talk about close friends. Surprisingly tactical underneath the soft exterior — she's run the numbers on exactly how much fog it takes to ruin a ranged attacker's day. Doesn't rattle easily; the air was never going to listen to her shouting at it, so she stopped shouting at anything.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Invisibility vs Humidity. Takazuki's biggest asset is not being seen — Mizuhana's fog beads on skin and clothing, outlining the shape of anything moving through it, invisible or not. The fight is about whether Takazuki can stay out of the fogbank entirely, which is a smaller battlefield than usual.
students.sports_festival_role: Quietly one of the most dangerous students at the Festival in any enclosed group event — a fogbank reshapes visibility for the entire field, not just her immediate area. In the tournament bracket, her concentration requirement is the obvious target; break her focus and the fog clears.
students.tier1_appearance: The practice yard fills with unscheduled ground fog for exactly four minutes during her lunch break. No weather warning was issued. She apologises to a groundskeeper, who has stopped asking questions about it.
students.dm_notes: Mizuhana works best as a slow-building threat — give the fog time to visibly form before it matters, then let it dominate the back half of an encounter. Her concentration dependency is the fair counterplay; telegraph it so players learn to look for the opening.
signature_moves: Fogbank (Action, concentration): 20-ft radius heavily obscuring fog for up to one minute.
Wring Dry (Action, within an active Fogbank): 15-ft radius CON save or 3d8 damage and a level of exhaustion.
Clear Sight (Passive): she and allies within 5 feet of her can see normally through her own Fogbank.

students.name: Hirosegawa Daichi

quirk_mechanics.weakness: He must maintain line of sight and concentration on the marked point itself, not a creature — if he loses sight of the exact point or his concentration breaks, the anchor releases immediately.

abilities.name: Mark
abilities.description: Designates a point in space within 60 feet he can see as anchored, for as long as he maintains concentration (up to one minute).

abilities.name: Recall
abilities.description: Any creature that moves more than 15 feet from the anchored point must succeed on a Wisdom save or be yanked back to the point, taking 1d10 force damage from the impact.

students.quirk_summary: Hirosegawa can anchor a single point in space through sustained eye contact and concentration — not a person, a location. Anything that tries to move away from that point gets pulled back, hard. It's a leash on geography rather than on a body, and it means the fight is never really about who he's looking at — it's about where he decided the fight happens.
students.personality: Intense, focused to the point of unnerving, rarely blinks during a conversation that matters to him (which is most of them, as far as anyone can tell). Doesn't do small talk well. Genuinely cares about his classmates in a way that comes out as overprotective vigilance rather than warmth.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Poltergeist vs Fixed Point. Nomi doesn't need to move to be dangerous — she can hurl objects around the battlefield without her own body going anywhere, which makes anchoring a point almost beside it: she just throws things at whoever's stuck there. Hirosegawa's whole strategy needs a rethink against her, and he knows it, which makes this the rivalry he respects most and trusts least.
students.sports_festival_role: A precision tool against any single dangerous target he can pin to a location — exactly what you want against a Festival favourite, exactly useless against anyone who fights through telekinesis or ranged effects rather than movement. In the tournament bracket, he's the student most likely to be intentionally paired against whoever the bracket considers the biggest threat.
students.tier1_appearance: A 1-A student in a hallway suddenly finds themselves yanked back a full step for no visible reason, looks around in confusion, and Hirosegawa is already walking away by the time they figure out who did it.
students.dm_notes: Hirosegawa is a single-point control specialist; he should feel oppressive against anyone forced to fight near his anchor and irrelevant against anyone who fights from range. His rivalry with Nomi is conceptual — a control specialist meeting the one archetype his control doesn't really touch.
signature_moves: Mark (Action, concentration): anchors a point within 60ft for up to one minute.
Recall (Passive, while a Mark is active): creatures moving more than 15ft from the anchored point make a WIS save or are yanked back, taking 1d10 force damage.
Unblinking (Passive): advantage on checks/saves to maintain concentration against effects that would force him to look away.

students.name: Natsukawa Riho

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Her clay reserve is finite and regenerates slowly — roughly one construct's worth every hour of rest — and anything she shapes crumbles to inert dust after about an hour, whether it's been used or not.

abilities.name: Shape
abilities.description: Secretes and instantly hardens a lump of dense, clay-like material from her palms into a rigid construct — a blade, a shield, a tool — that functions mechanically as that item for one hour.

abilities.name: Reshape
abilities.description: Unshapes and reshapes an existing construct into a different form without needing a fresh action.

students.quirk_summary: Natsukawa's palms produce a dense, clay-like substance that hardens to a rigid, functional shape the instant she finishes forming it — a blade, a shield, a makeshift tool, whatever the moment calls for. Unlike a crafter who needs raw material lying around, she brings her own; the tradeoff is that her reserve is limited and slow to replenish, so she thinks hard about what's actually worth making before she commits to it.
students.personality: Meticulous, a little precious about her materials, will absolutely lecture you about the correct way to condition clay before shaping it. Quietly proud of a craft that most people dismiss as cute. Funny about it in a self-aware way — she knows exactly how this looks and has stopped caring what people think.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Hologram vs Kiln. Both build things that aren't quite what they first appear to be — Ichitaka's projections trick the eye, Natsukawa's constructs are real and load-bearing the moment you touch them. The fight is a question of whether Ichitaka's illusions can bait Natsukawa into wasting one of her limited constructs on something that turns out to be fake.
students.sports_festival_role: Versatile and resourceful in objective-based events — whatever the problem is, she can probably shape a tool for it, within her reserve. In the tournament bracket, opponents who can force her to burn through her limited supply early put her at a real, discoverable disadvantage.
students.tier1_appearance: A small clay bird is found sitting on a 1-A student's desk, and on close inspection its wingtip is honed sharp enough to have actually scored the wood slightly. Nobody saw her do it.
students.dm_notes: Natsukawa rewards creative DMing — let players describe an unusual problem and have her improvise a construct for it. Her limitation (finite reserve, hour-long lifespan) keeps her grounded; track how much she's used in a given session.
signature_moves: Shape (Action): forms a construct — weapon, shield, or tool — from her own material, lasting one hour.
Reshape (Bonus Action): reforms an existing construct into a different one instantly.
Fired Edge (Passive): bladed constructs deal 1d6 slashing damage and ignore the first point of an opponent's natural armor bonus.

students.name: Kuromine Sosuke

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Only affects creatures capable of hearing him and only works at conversational range — loud environments that drown out his own rhythm-setting, or targets that are deafened, are immune.

abilities.name: Set the Tempo
abilities.description: Targets a creature within 30 feet, imposing his internal rhythm on their reactions. Target makes a Wisdom save; on a failure, choose one: their speed is halved until the start of their next turn (off-beat), or their next attack roll before the start of their next turn has disadvantage (rushed).

abilities.name: Downbeat
abilities.description: When a creature currently affected by his Set the Tempo makes an attack roll, he can force it to reroll and take the worse result.

students.quirk_summary: Kuromine perceives and can impose tempo — a rhythm that gets inside a target's reactions and either slows them down or rushes them into overcommitting. He doesn't need contact or a device, just a target who can hear him keep the beat. He's spent years learning to read someone's natural rhythm before he changes it, which is most of the actual skill involved.
students.personality: Cool and a little aloof on the surface, genuinely enthusiastic underneath about anything mechanical or rhythmic. Listens more than he talks. Has a habit of tapping a beat against his own leg when he's thinking, which classmates have learned means don't interrupt yet.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Twin Impact vs Metronome. Toragi's twin-strike relies on precise internal timing — exactly the kind of rhythm Kuromine's quirk is built to disrupt from the outside. The fight comes down to whether he can get his tempo into her head before her own timing wins out.
students.sports_festival_role: Strong in prolonged one-on-one exchanges where disrupting an opponent's rhythm compounds over time. In the tournament bracket, opponents who fight from a distance he can't be heard at, or who don't rely on precise timing to begin with, are much harder for him to touch.
students.tier1_appearance: A sparring partner reports that their footwork kept 'feeling wrong' during a drill, half a beat off from where it should have landed, the whole time Kuromine was standing nearby tapping his leg.
students.dm_notes: Kuromine plays like a debuff specialist — his effect compounds the longer he stays in the fight uninterrupted. Let smart players shut him down by getting out of earshot or overwhelming the environment with noise. His quiet rivalry-of-craft with Kitamura — both precision setup specialists in their own way — is a nice beat to use in a shared scene if both classes cross paths.
signature_moves: Set the Tempo (Action): target within 30ft makes a WIS save or suffers halved speed or disadvantage on their next attack, his choice.
Downbeat (Reaction, 6th level): forces a currently-affected target to reroll an attack and take the worse result.
Perfect Pitch (Passive): advantage on checks to notice or track a creature by sound alone.

students.name: Wakatabi Senri

quirk_mechanics.weakness: The stored damage must be spent as a single melee strike delivered personally — if she's incapacitated, restrained, or can't reach a target before the end of her next turn after banking it, the stored damage dissipates harmlessly.

abilities.name: Bank It
abilities.description: When hit by an attack, negates all damage from it and instead stores the amount as banked force, up to a maximum equal to twice her level.

abilities.name: Collect
abilities.description: Makes a melee attack against any creature; on a hit, adds all currently banked force to the damage as a single lump payment, then resets banked force to zero.

students.quirk_summary: Wakatabi can shrug off an attack that would have hit her and store the force instead of taking the damage — then deliver it all back later, in person, through her fists. It only works reactively, on attacks that actually land, which means she has to be willing to get hit on purpose more often than most people would like, and patient enough to wait for the right moment to collect.
students.personality: Fearless in a slightly worrying way — getting hit is half her kit, so she stops flinching from it long before her classmates do. Blunt, encouraging, the person who tells you to take the hit and trust the plan. People do, mostly because it's worked so far.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Neutralization vs Debt Collector. Kinosho can shut down a quirk on contact — and Wakatabi's entire kit depends on the quirk being active the moment she's hit. If Kinosho lands the neutralizing touch first, Wakatabi just takes the damage like anyone else, with nothing banked to collect on. The whole fight is a race to see who touches whom in what order.
students.sports_festival_role: Punishing in any event where opponents commit to a few big hits, since all of that damage eventually comes back at once, on her schedule. In the tournament bracket, opponents who use sustained, low-damage pressure rather than big single attacks deny her the leverage she needs to bank anything worth collecting.
students.tier1_appearance: A sparring partner's full-strength kick lands clean on Wakatabi. Nothing happens. Two exchanges later it happens to them instead, all at once, and they check their own ribs, confused about the delay.
students.dm_notes: Wakatabi is a high-skill-expression reactive fighter — she's only as good as the attacks she's allowed to bank and the openings she gets to collect on. Her rivalry with Kinosho is a clean hard-counter dynamic; let that be the explicit tension if they ever meet on-screen.
signature_moves: Bank It (Reaction): negates an attack's damage, storing it as banked force up to twice her level.
Collect (Action): melee attack that adds all banked force as bonus damage on a hit, then resets to zero.
No Flinch (Passive): immune to being frightened by an attack she intends to bank.

students.name: Ibarada Shun

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Touch is required to strip friction and inertia control from a target, and the effect only lasts while he maintains concentration — releasing concentration returns normal physics to the target instantly, wherever its momentum has carried it.

abilities.name: Frictionless
abilities.description: Touches a creature or object up to Large size, removing its ability to control its own friction and inertia for as long as he maintains concentration (up to one minute). Any force applied to it — a push, a gust, its own momentum — continues unopposed until something solid stops it or the effect ends.

abilities.name: Dead Stop
abilities.description: When a creature affected by Frictionless would collide with something at high speed, he can end the effect early to restore normal friction just before impact, halving the resulting damage.

students.quirk_summary: Ibarada can touch a creature or object and strip away its grip on its own momentum — once he's done it, anything that was already moving keeps moving, and anything pushed keeps sliding, until something stops it or he lets go. On himself he barely uses it; on something large and already committed to a direction, one touch turns their own momentum into the problem.
students.personality: Calm to the point of seeming detached, picks his moments rather than his fights. Doesn't enjoy conflict for its own sake but has a sharp, dry sense of when to act. Tends to be underestimated by people who don't realize how much of the fight is over the moment he gets a hand on you.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Dragon vs Unmoored. Tazato's draconic form is huge, fast, and built around controlled, powerful momentum — exactly what Ibarada's quirk is designed to take out of her hands. One clean touch and she can't stop, can't turn, can't do anything but keep going in whatever direction she committed to. The trick is getting that touch on something that large and that dangerous before it's already moving too fast to matter.
students.sports_festival_role: A precision answer to any large, fast, or momentum-committed opponent — genuinely frightening once he closes the distance. In the tournament bracket, the entire fight against him is about denying him that first touch, because everything after it goes his way.
students.tier1_appearance: A dropped textbook in the library hallway keeps sliding along the floor in a dead straight line long after it should have stopped, and Ibarada, walking past without slowing, catches it with a foot at the last second.
students.dm_notes: Ibarada is a control specialist whose entire threat profile hinges on landing one touch. Play him as patient and opportunistic rather than aggressive — he waits for the opening rather than forcing it. His rivalry with Tazato is the clean 'the bigger and faster they are, the worse it goes' dynamic.
signature_moves: Frictionless (Action, concentration): touch a creature or object up to Large size, removing its control over its own friction and momentum for up to one minute.
Dead Stop (Reaction, 5th level): ends Frictionless early to halve impact damage from a resulting collision.
Light Touch (Passive): advantage on grapple checks made to establish the initial touch required for Frictionless.
